fs-bc-never-run.front: Rule one with bears and cougars?

fs-bc-why.front: Why do hunters meet more bears?
fs-bc-why.back: Quiet movement, dawn and dusk, blood and gut piles, calls and decoys, thick cover, kill sites.
fs-bc-why.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Why hunters meet more bears: we move quietly, we hunt dawn and dusk when bears move, we carry blood and gut piles that smell like food, calls and decoys sound like food, we walk thick cover with short sight lines, and bears claim kill sites. Do the opposite where you can.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Why hunters meet more bears</text><rect x="20" y="48" width="112" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" width="112" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="201" y="178" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Thick cover</text><text fs-bc-noise.back: Near running water, thick brush, berry patches and in high wind.

fs-bc-carcass.front: You find a carcass you did not shoot. What do you do?
fs-bc-carcass.back: Leave the area at once and report it. A bear may be guarding it.

fs-bc-aware.front: Bear sees you but is calm?
fs-bc-aware.back: Speak softly and back away slowly. Do not follow it.

fs-bc-approach.front: Bear keeps coming steadily toward you?
fs-bc-approach.back: May be predatory. Yell, stand big, move to high ground, spray, be ready to fight.

fs-bc-spray-range.front: At what distance does WildSafeBC say to spray?
fs-bc-spray-range.back: When the bear is within about 5 to 10 m.

fs-bc-spray-where.front: Where do you carry bear spray?
fs-bc-spray-where.back: Chest or hip holster. Never in the pack.

fs-bc-spray-gun.front: Spray or gun: which stopped bears more often in studies?
fs-bc-spray-gun.back: Spray: about 92% versus about 67% for guns (as reported for the Smith and Herrero studies).
fs-bc-spray-gun.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Bar chart: bear spray stopped aggressive bear behaviour in about 92 percent of cases; firearms in about 67 percent, as reported in coverage of the Smith and Herrero studies.   <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Bear spray vs firearms (studies)</text><text x="70" y="108" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">Spray</text><rect x="80" y="80" width="258" height="40" rx="4" fill="#2e7d32"/><text x="348" y="108" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">92%</text><text x="70" y="178" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">Guns</text><rect x="80" y="150" width="188" height="40" rx="4" fill="#9a9a8f"/><text x="278" y="178" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">67%</text><text x="200" y="240" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Stopped the bear, as reported in</text><text x="200" y="258" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">coverage of Smith and Herrero studies</text><text x="200" y="290" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Carry spray. fs-bc-defensive.front: Defensive bear makes contact. What do you do?
fs-bc-defensive.back: Lie on your stomach, pack on, hands over the back of your neck, legs apart. Stay still until it leaves.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Defensive bear contact position: lie on your stomach with your pack on, hands clasped over the back of your neck, legs spread so it is hard to flip you. Stay still until the bear leaves.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>

fs-bc-gutpile.front: How far from the gut pile should the meat go?
fs-bc-gutpile.back: At least 200 m (Alberta guidance). Bears often go to the gut pile first.

  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">2. fs-bc-hang.front: How high and how far from trunks do you hang meat?
fs-bc-hang.back: At least 3.5 m up and 1.5 m from tree trunks, in view from a distance.

fs-bc-return.front: Going back to your meat: how?
fs-bc-return.back: From upwind, stop and glass it, call out. Bear on it, or moved or buried: leave and report.

fs-bc-drag.front: Drag the carcass back to camp?
fs-bc-drag.back: No. It lays a scent trail to where you sleep.

fs-bc-camp.back: Food, cooking and meat at least 100 m from where you sleep. Never food in the tent.
